# 7 Reset and clock control (RCC)

## 7.1 Reset

There are three types of reset, defined as system reset, power reset and RTC domain reset.

### 7.1.1 Power reset

A power reset is generated when one of the following events occurs:

1. Power-on reset (POR) or brown-out reset (BOR)
2. When exiting from Standby mode
3. When exiting from Shutdown mode

A brown-out reset, including power-on or power-down reset (POR/PDR), sets all registers to their reset values except the RTC domain.

When exiting Standby mode, all registers in the VCORE domain are set to their reset value. Registers outside the VCORE domain (RTC, WKUP, IWDG, and Standby/Shutdown modes control) are not impacted.

When exiting Shutdown mode, a brown-out reset is generated, resetting all registers except those in the RTC domain.

### 7.1.2 System reset

A system reset sets all registers to their reset values unless specified otherwise in the register description. This reset is generated when one of the following events occurs:

1. A low level on the NRST pin (external reset)
2. Window watchdog event (WWDG reset)
3. Independent watchdog event (IWDG reset)
4. A software reset (SW reset) (see [Software reset](#XREF_55574__4_1_2_Software_reset15))
5. Low-power mode security reset (see [Low-power mode security reset](#XREF_67880__4_1_3_Low-power_management_reset15))
6. Option byte loader reset (see [Option byte loader reset](#XREF_37093__Option_byte_loader_reset15))
7. A brown-out reset

The reset source can be identified by checking the reset flags in the Control/Status register, RCC\_CSR (see [Section 7.4.28](#XREF_76073__3_1_24_Control/status_register_(RCC_CSR)15)).

#### NRST pin (external reset)

Through specific option bits (NRST\_MODE), the NRST pin is configurable for operating as:

- Reset input/output (default at device delivery)  
  Any valid reset signal on the pin is propagated to device internal logic and all internal reset sources are externally driven through a pulse generator to this pin. The GPIO functionality (PG10) is not available. The pulse generator guarantees a minimum reset pulse duration of 20 µs for each internal reset source to be output on the NRST pin. An internal reset holder option can be used, if enabled in the option bytes, to ensure that the pin is pulled low until its voltage meets VIL threshold. This function guarantee the detection of internal reset sources by external components when the line faces a significant capacitive load. In case on an internal reset, the internal pull-up RPU is deactivated in order to save the power consumption through the pull-up resistor. This mode is always active (independently of the option bytes setting) during each device power-on-reset (until option bytes are loaded): power on the device or wake up from Shutdown mode.
- Reset input  
  In this mode, any valid reset signal on the NRST pin is propagated to device internal logic, but resets generated internally by the device are not visible on the pin. In this configuration, GPIO functionality (PG10) is not available.
- GPIO  
  In this mode, the pin can be used as PG10 standard GPIO. The reset function of the pin is not available. Reset is only possible from device internal reset sources and it is not propagated to the pin.

#### Figure 16. Simplified diagram of the reset circuit![MSv40966V2](MSv40966V2.svg)

<a id="XREF_55574__4_1_2_Software_reset15"></a>

#### Software reset

The SYSRESETREQ bit in Cortex®-M4 with FPU Application Interrupt and Reset Control Register must be set to force a software reset on the device (refer to the STM32F3xx/F4xx/L4xx Cortex®-M4 programming manual (PM0214)).

<a id="XREF_67880__4_1_3_Low-power_management_reset15"></a>

#### Low-power mode security reset

To prevent that critical applications mistakenly enter a low-power mode, two low-power mode security resets are available. If enabled in option bytes, the resets are generated in the following conditions:

1. Entering Standby mode: this type of reset is enabled by resetting nRST\_STDBY bit in User option Bytes. In this case, whenever a Standby mode entry sequence is successfully executed, the device is reset instead of entering Standby mode.
2. Entering Stop mode: this type of reset is enabled by resetting nRST\_STOP bit in User option bytes. In this case, whenever a Stop mode entry sequence is successfully executed, the device is reset instead of entering Stop mode.
3. Entering Shutdown mode: this type of reset is enabled by resetting nRST\_SHDW bit in User option bytes. In this case, whenever a Shutdown mode entry sequence is successfully executed, the device is reset instead of entering Shutdown mode.

For further information on the user option bytes refer to [Section 3.4.1](Embedded_flash_memory_%28FLASH%29_for_category_3_devices.md#XREF_45490__3_4_1_Option_bytes_description13).

<a id="XREF_37093__Option_byte_loader_reset15"></a>

#### Option byte loader reset

The option byte loader reset is generated when the OBL\_LAUNCH bit (bit 27) is set in the FLASH\_CR register. This bit is used to launch the option byte loading by software.

<a id="XREF_25576__4_1_2_Power_reset15"></a>

### 7.1.3 RTC domain reset

The RTC domain has two specific resets.

A RTC domain reset is generated when one of the following events occurs:

1. Software reset, triggered by setting the BDRST bit in the [RTC domain control register (RCC\_BDCR)](#XREF_22571__7_4_29_Backup_domain_control_register_(RCC_BDCR)15).
2. VDD or VBAT power on, if both supplies have previously been powered off.

A RTC domain reset only affects the LSE oscillator, the RTC, the Backup registers and the RCC RTC domain control register.

## 7.2 Clocks

Three different clock sources can be used to drive the system clock (SYSCLK):

- HSI16 (high speed internal)16 MHz RC oscillator clock
- HSE oscillator clock, from 4 to 48 MHz
- PLL clock

The HSI16 is used as system clock source after startup from Reset.

The devices have the following additional clock sources:

- 32 kHz low speed internal RC (LSI RC) which drives the independent watchdog and optionally the RTC used for Auto-wake-up from Stop and Standby modes.
- 32.768 kHz low speed external crystal (LSE crystal) which optionally drives the real-time clock (RTCCLK).
- RC 48 MHz internal clock sources (HSI48) to potentially drive the USB FS and the RNG.

Each clock source can be switched on or off independently when it is not used, to optimize power consumption.

Several prescalers can be used to configure the AHB frequency, the APB1 and APB2 domains. The maximum frequency of AHB, APB1, and APB2 domains is 170 MHz.

All the peripheral clocks are derived from their bus clock (HCLK, PCLK1 or PCLK2) except:

- The 48 MHz clock, used for USB device FS, and RNG. This clock is derived (selected by software) from one of the four following sources:
<br>- PLL “Q” clock
<br>- HSI48 internal oscillator

When available, the HSI48 48 MHz clock can be coupled to the clock recovery system allowing adequate clock connection for the USB OTG FS (Crystal less solution).

- The ADCs clock which is derived (selected by software) from one of the following sources:
<br>- System clock (SYSCLK)
<br>- PLL “P” clock
- The U(S)ARTs clocks which are derived (selected by software) from one of the four following sources:
<br>- System clock (SYSCLK)
<br>- HSI16 clock
<br>- LSE clock
<br>- APB1 or APB2 clock (PCLK1 or PCLK2 depending on which APB is mapped the U(S)ART)

The wake-up from Stop mode is supported only when the clock is HSI16 or LSE.

- The I2Cs clocks which are derived (selected by software) from one of the three following sources:
<br>- System clock (SYSCLK)
<br>- HSI16 clock
<br>- APB1 clock (PCLK1)

The wake-up from Stop mode is supported only when the clock is HSI16.

- The SAI1 clock which is derived (selected by software) from one of the following sources:
<br>- an external clock mapped on I2S\_CKIN
<br>- System clock
<br>- PLL “Q” clock
<br>- HSI16 clock
- The QUADSPI kernel clock which is derived (selected by software) from one of the following sources:
<br>- System clock,
<br>- PLL “Q” clock
<br>- HSI16 clock
- The low-power timer (LPTIM1) clock which is derived (selected by software) from one of the five following sources:
<br>- LSI clock
<br>- LSE clock
<br>- HSI16 clock
<br>- APB1 clock (PCLK1)
<br>- External clock mapped on LPTIMx\_IN1

The functionality in Stop mode (including wake-up) is supported only when the clock is LSI or LSE, or in external clock mode.

- The RTC clock which is derived (selected by software) from one of the three following sources:
<br>- LSE clock
<br>- LSI clock
<br>- HSE clock divided by 32

The functionality in Stop mode (including wake-up) is supported only when the clock is LSI or LSE.

- The IWDG clock which is always the LSI clock.
- The UCPD1 clock, which is derived from HSI16 clock.
- The FDCAN1 clock, which is derived (selected by software) from one of the two following sources:
<br>- HSE clock
<br>- PLL “Q” clock
<br>- PCLK clock

The RCC feeds the Cortex® System Timer (SysTick) external clock with the AHB clock (HCLK) divided by 8. The SysTick can work either with this clock or directly with the Cortex® clock (HCLK), configurable in the SysTick Control and Status Register.

FCLK acts as Cortex®-M4 with FPU free-running clock. For more details refer to the Cortex®-M4 programming manual (PM0214).

<a id="XREF_22097__Figure_2__Clock_tree15"></a>

1.For full details about the internal and external clock source characteristics, refer to the “Electrical characteristics” section of the datasheet.

2.The ADC clock can be derived from the AHB clock of the ADC bus interface, divided by a programmable factor (1, 2 or 4). When the programmable factor is 1, the AHB prescaler must be equal to 1.

### 7.2.1 HSE clock

The high speed external clock signal (HSE) can be generated from two possible clock sources:

- HSE external crystal/ceramic resonator
- HSE user external clock

The resonator and the load capacitors have to be placed as close as possible to the oscillator pins to minimize output distortion and startup stabilization time. The loading capacitance values must be adjusted according to the selected oscillator.

<a id="XREF_49937__Table_1__ST7_Clock_Sources15"></a>

#### Figure 18. 

<div align="center"><table class="TableTitle"><col width="121.80px"/><col width="416.78px"/><thead><tr height="28.00px"><th><p class="TableHeadC">Clock source</p></th><th><p class="TableHeadC">Hardware configuration</p></th></tr></thead><tr height="166.33px"><td><p class="TableBodyC">External clock</p></td><td><p class="Anchor">          <img class="imageSettings" height="142.330912" src="MSv31915V1.svg" style="display:block;margin:auto;" type="image/svg+xml" width="400.857361"/></p></td></tr><tr height="184.82px"><td><p class="TableBodyC">Crystal/Ceramic resonators</p></td><td><p class="Anchor">          <img class="imageSettings" height="160.815450" src="MSv31916V1.svg" style="display:block;margin:auto;" type="image/svg+xml" width="398.774841"/></p></td></tr></table></div>

 HSE/ LSE clock sources

#### External crystal/ceramic resonator (HSE crystal)

The 4 to 48 MHz external oscillator has the advantage of producing a very accurate rate on the main clock. The associated hardware configuration is shown in [Figure 18](#XREF_49937__Table_1__ST7_Clock_Sources15). Refer to the electrical characteristics section of the datasheet for more details.

The HSERDY flag in the [Clock control register (RCC\_CR)](#XREF_15554__2_2_6_Clock_control_register_(CLK_CR)15) indicates if the HSE oscillator is stable or not. At startup, the clock is not released until this bit is set by hardware. An interrupt can be generated if enabled in the [Clock interrupt enable register (RCC\_CIER)](#XREF_20430__2_2_8_Clock_interrupt_register_(CLK_IR)15).

The HSE Crystal can be switched on and off using the HSEON bit in the [Clock control register (RCC\_CR)](#XREF_15554__2_2_6_Clock_control_register_(CLK_CR)15).

#### External source (HSE bypass)

In this mode, an external clock source must be provided. It can have a frequency of up to 48 MHz. You select this mode by setting the HSEBYP and HSEON bits in the [Clock control register (RCC\_CR)](#XREF_15554__2_2_6_Clock_control_register_(CLK_CR)15). The external clock signal (square, sinus or triangle) with ~40-60 % duty cycle depending on the frequency (refer to the datasheet) has to drive the OSC\_IN pin while the OSC\_OUT pin can be used as GPIO. See [Figure 18](#XREF_49937__Table_1__ST7_Clock_Sources15).

### 7.2.2 HSI16 clock

The HSI16 clock signal is generated from an internal 16 MHz RC Oscillator.

The HSI16 RC oscillator has the advantage of providing a clock source at low cost (no external components). It also has a faster startup time than the HSE crystal oscillator however, even with calibration the frequency is less accurate than an external crystal oscillator or ceramic resonator.

The HSI16 clock can be selected as system clock after wake-up from Stop modes (Stop 0, Stop 1), see [Section 7.3](#XREF_24698__7_2_12_Internal/external_clock_measurement_with_TIM9/TIM10/TIM11%0D15). It can also be used as a backup clock source (auxiliary clock) if the HSE crystal oscillator fails. Refer to [Section 7.2.9](#XREF_69501__2_3_Clock_security_system_(CSS)15).

#### Calibration

RC oscillator frequencies can vary from one chip to another due to manufacturing process variations, this is why each device is factory calibrated by ST for 1 % accuracy at TA=25°C.

After reset, the factory calibration value is loaded in the HSICAL[7:0] bits in the [Internal clock sources calibration register (RCC\_ICSCR)](#XREF_58218__7_4_2_Internal_clock_sources_calibration_register_(RCC_ICSCR)15).

If the application is subject to voltage or temperature variations this may affect the RC oscillator speed. You can trim the HSI16 frequency in the application using the HSITRIM[6:0] in the [Internal clock sources calibration register (RCC\_ICSCR)](#XREF_58218__7_4_2_Internal_clock_sources_calibration_register_(RCC_ICSCR)15).

For more details on how to measure the HSI16 frequency variation, refer to [Section 7.2.16](#XREF_11631__7_2_12_Internal/external_clock_measurement_with_TIM1615).

The HSIRDY flag in the [Clock control register (RCC\_CR)](#XREF_15554__2_2_6_Clock_control_register_(CLK_CR)15) indicates if the HSI16 oscillator is stable or not. At startup, the HSI16 output clock is not released until this bit is set by hardware.

The HSI16 oscillator can be switched on and off using the HSION bit in the [Clock control register (RCC\_CR)](#XREF_15554__2_2_6_Clock_control_register_(CLK_CR)15).

The HSI16 signal can also be used as a backup source (Auxiliary clock) if the HSE crystal oscillator fails. Refer to [Section 7.2.9](#XREF_69501__2_3_Clock_security_system_(CSS)15).

### 7.2.3 HSI48 clock

The HSI48 clock signal is generated from an internal 48 MHz RC oscillator and can be used directly for USB and for random number generator (RNG).

The internal 48 MHz RC oscillator is mainly dedicated to provide a high precision clock to the USB peripheral by means of a special Clock Recovery System (CRS) circuitry. The CRS can use the LSE or an external signal to automatically and quickly adjust the oscillator frequency on-fly. It is disabled as soon as the system enters Stop or Standby mode. When the CRS is not used, the HSI48 RC oscillator runs on its default frequency which is subject to manufacturing process variations.

The HSI48RDY flag in the Clock recovery RC register (RCC\_CRRCR) indicates whether the HSI48 RC oscillator is stable or not. At startup, the HSI48 RC oscillator output clock is not released until this bit is set by hardware.

The HSI48 can be switched on and off using the HSI48ON bit in the Clock recovery RC register (RCC\_CRRCR).

### 7.2.4 PLL

The internal PLL can be used to multiply the HSI16 or HSE output clock frequency. The PLL input frequency must be within the range defined in the device datasheet. The selected clock source is divided by a programmable factor PLLM from 1 to 8 to provide a clock frequency in the requested input range. Refer to [Figure 17](#XREF_22097__Figure_2__Clock_tree15) and [PLL configuration register (RCC\_PLLCFGR)](#XREF_26045__7_4_4_PLL_configuration_register_(RCC_PLLCFGR)15).

The PLL configuration (selection of the input clock and multiplication factor) must be done before enabling the PLL. Once the PLL is enabled, these parameters cannot be changed.

To modify the PLL configuration, proceed as follows:

1. Disable the PLL by setting PLLON to 0 in [Clock control register (RCC\_CR)](#XREF_15554__2_2_6_Clock_control_register_(CLK_CR)15).
2. Wait until PLLRDY is cleared. The PLL is now fully stopped.
3. Change the desired parameter.
4. Enable the PLL again by setting PLLON to 1.
5. Enable the desired PLL outputs by configuring PLLPEN, PLLQEN, PLLREN in [PLL configuration register (RCC\_PLLCFGR)](#XREF_26045__7_4_4_PLL_configuration_register_(RCC_PLLCFGR)15).

An interrupt can be generated when the PLL is ready, if enabled in the [Clock interrupt enable register (RCC\_CIER)](#XREF_20430__2_2_8_Clock_interrupt_register_(CLK_IR)15).

The PLL output frequency must not exceed 170 MHz.

The enable bit of each PLL output clock (PLLPEN, PLLQEN, PLLREN) can be modified at any time without stopping the corresponding PLL. PLLREN cannot be cleared if PLLCLK is used as system clock.

### 7.2.5 LSE clock

The LSE crystal is a 32.768 kHz Low Speed External crystal or ceramic resonator. It has the advantage of providing a low-power but highly accurate clock source to the real-time clock peripheral (RTC) for clock/calendar or other timing functions.

The LSE crystal is switched on and off using the LSEON bit in [RTC domain control register (RCC\_BDCR)](#XREF_22571__7_4_29_Backup_domain_control_register_(RCC_BDCR)15). The crystal oscillator driving strength can be changed at runtime using the LSEDRV[1:0] bits in the [RTC domain control register (RCC\_BDCR)](#XREF_22571__7_4_29_Backup_domain_control_register_(RCC_BDCR)15) to obtain the best compromise between robustness and short start-up time on one side and low-power-consumption on the other side. The LSE drive can be decreased to the lower drive capability (LSEDRV = 00) when the LSE is ON. However, once LSEDRV is selected, the drive capability can not be increased if LSEON = 1.

The LSERDY flag in the [RTC domain control register (RCC\_BDCR)](#XREF_22571__7_4_29_Backup_domain_control_register_(RCC_BDCR)15) indicates whether the LSE crystal is stable or not. At startup, the LSE crystal output clock signal is not released until this bit is set by hardware. An interrupt can be generated if enabled in the [Clock interrupt enable register (RCC\_CIER)](#XREF_20430__2_2_8_Clock_interrupt_register_(CLK_IR)15).

#### External source (LSE bypass)

In this mode, an external clock source must be provided. It can have a frequency of up to 1 MHz. You select this mode by setting the LSEBYP and LSEON bits in the [AHB1 peripheral clocks enable in Sleep and Stop modes register (RCC\_AHB1SMENR)](#XREF_45997__2_1_23_Backup_domain_control_register_(RCC_BDCR)15). The external clock signal (square, sinus or triangle) with ~50 % duty cycle has to drive the OSC32\_IN pin while the OSC32\_OUT pin can be used as GPIO. See [Figure 18](#XREF_49937__Table_1__ST7_Clock_Sources15).

### 7.2.6 LSI clock

The LSI RC acts as a low-power clock source that can be kept running in Stop and Standby mode for the independent watchdog (IWDG) and RTC. The clock frequency is 32 kHz. For more details, refer to the electrical characteristics section of the datasheets.

The LSI RC can be switched on and off using the LSION bit in the [Control/status register (RCC\_CSR)](#XREF_76073__3_1_24_Control/status_register_(RCC_CSR)15).

The LSIRDY flag in the [Control/status register (RCC\_CSR)](#XREF_76073__3_1_24_Control/status_register_(RCC_CSR)15) indicates if the LSI oscillator is stable or not. At startup, the clock is not released until this bit is set by hardware. An interrupt can be generated if enabled in the [Clock interrupt enable register (RCC\_CIER)](#XREF_20430__2_2_8_Clock_interrupt_register_(CLK_IR)15).

### 7.2.7 System clock (SYSCLK) selection

Four different clock sources can be used to drive the system clock (SYSCLK):

- HSI16 oscillator
- HSE oscillator
- PLL

The system clock maximum frequency is 170 MHz. After a system reset, the HSI16 oscillator is selected as system clock. When a clock source is used directly or through the PLL as a system clock, it is not possible to stop it.

A switch from one clock source to another occurs only if the target clock source is ready (clock stable after startup delay or PLL locked). If a clock source which is not yet ready is selected, the switch occurs when the clock source becomes ready. Status bits in the RCC\_CR and RCC\_CFGR registers indicate which clock(s) is (are) ready and which clock is currently used as a system clock.

To switch from low speed to high speed or from high speed to low speed system clock, it is recommended to use a transition state with medium speed clock, for at least 1 µs.

Clock source switching conditions:

- Switching from HSE or HSI16 to PLL with AHB frequency (HCLK) higher than 80 MHz
- Switching from PLL with HCLK higher than 80 MHz to HSE or HSI16

Transition state:

- Set the AHB prescaler HPRE[3:0] bits to divide the system frequency by 2
- Switch system clock to PLL
- Wait at least 1 µs and then reconfigure AHB prescaler bits to the needed HCLK frequency

### 7.2.9 Clock security system (CSS)

Clock Security System can be activated by software. In this case, the clock detector is enabled after the HSE oscillator startup delay, and disabled when this oscillator is stopped.

If a failure is detected on the HSE clock, the HSE oscillator is automatically disabled, a clock failure event is sent to the break input of the advanced-control timers (TIM1/TIM8/TIM20 and TIM15/16/17) and to the hrtim\_sys\_flt, and an interrupt is generated to inform the software about the failure (Clock Security System Interrupt CSSI), allowing the MCU to perform rescue operations. The CSSI is linked to the Cortex®-M4 with FPU NMI (Non-Maskable Interrupt) exception vector.

**Note:**

Once the CSS is enabled and if the HSE clock fails, the CSS interrupt occurs and a NMI is automatically generated. The NMI is executed indefinitely unless the CSS interrupt pending bit is cleared. As a consequence, in the NMI ISR user must clear the CSS interrupt by setting the CSSC bit in the [Clock interrupt clear register (RCC\_CICR)](#XREF_47307__7_4_9_Clock_interrupt_clear_register_(RCC_CICR)15).

If the HSE oscillator is used directly or indirectly as the system clock (indirectly means: it is used as PLL input clock, and the PLL clock is used as system clock), a detected failure causes a switch of the system clock to the HSI16 oscillator, and the disabling of the HSE oscillator. If the HSE clock (divided or not) is the clock entry of the PLL used as system clock when the failure occurs, the PLL is disabled too.

### 7.2.10 Clock security system on LSE

A Clock Security System on LSE can be activated by software writing the LSECSSON bit in the [Control/status register (RCC\_CSR)](#XREF_76073__3_1_24_Control/status_register_(RCC_CSR)15). This bit can be disabled only by a hardware reset or RTC software reset, or after a failure detection on LSE. LSECSSON must be written after LSE and LSI are enabled (LSEON and LSION enabled) and ready (LSERDY and LSIRDY set by hardware), and after the RTC clock has been selected by RTCSEL.

The CSS on LSE is working in all modes except VBAT. It is working also under system reset (excluding power on reset). If a failure is detected on the external 32 kHz oscillator, the LSE clock is no longer supplied to the RTC but no hardware action is made to the registers. If the HSI16 was in PLL-mode, this mode is disabled.

In Standby mode a wake-up is generated. In other modes an interrupt can be sent to wake up the software (see [Clock interrupt enable register (RCC\_CIER)](#XREF_20430__2_2_8_Clock_interrupt_register_(CLK_IR)15), [Clock interrupt flag register (RCC\_CIFR)](#XREF_11076__7_4_8_Clock_interrupt_flag_register_(RCC_CIFR)15), [Clock interrupt clear register (RCC\_CICR)](#XREF_47307__7_4_9_Clock_interrupt_clear_register_(RCC_CICR)15)).

The software MUST then disable the LSECSSON bit, stop the defective 32 kHz oscillator (disabling LSEON), and change the RTC clock source (no clock or LSI or HSE, with RTCSEL), or take any required action to secure the application.

The frequency of LSE oscillator have to be higher than 30 kHz to avoid false positive CSS detection.

### 7.2.11 ADC clock

The ADC clock is derived from the system clock, or from the PLL “P” output. It can be divided by the following prescalers values: 1,2,4,6,8,10,12,16,32,64,128 or 256 by configuring the ADCx\_CCR register. It is asynchronous to the AHB clock. Alternatively, the ADC clock can be derived from the AHB clock of the ADC bus interface, divided by a programmable factor (1, 2 or 4). This programmable factor is configured using the CKMODE bit fields in the ADCx\_CCR.

If the programmed factor is 1, the AHB prescaler must be set to 1.

Refer to the device datasheet for the maximum ADC clock.

### 7.2.12 RTC clock

The RTCCLK clock source can be either the HSE/32, LSE or LSI clock. It is selected by programming the RTCSEL[1:0] bits in the [RTC domain control register (RCC\_BDCR)](#XREF_22571__7_4_29_Backup_domain_control_register_(RCC_BDCR)15). This selection cannot be modified without resetting the RTC domain. The system must always be configured so as to get a PCLK frequency greater then or equal to the RTCCLK frequency for a proper operation of the RTC.

The LSE clock is in the RTC domain, whereas the HSE and LSI clocks are not. Consequently:

- If LSE is selected as RTC clock:
<br>- The RTC continues to work even if the VDD supply is switched off, provided the VBAT supply is maintained.
- If LSI is selected as the RTC clock:
<br>- The RTC state is not guaranteed if the VDD supply is powered off.
- If the HSE clock divided by a prescaler is used as the RTC clock:
<br>- The RTC state is not guaranteed if the VDD supply is powered off or if the internal voltage regulator is powered off (removing power from the VCORE domain).

When the RTC clock is LSE or LSI, the RTC remains clocked and functional under system reset.

### 7.2.13 Timer clock

The timer clock frequencies (tim\_ker\_ck) are automatically defined by hardware. If the APB prescaler equals 1, the timer clock frequencies are set to the same frequency of the APB domain, otherwise, they are set to twice (×2) the frequency of the APB domain.

### 7.2.14 Watchdog clock

If the Independent watchdog (IWDG) is started by either hardware option or software access, the LSI oscillator is forced ON and cannot be disabled. After the LSI oscillator temporization, the clock is provided to the IWDG.

### 7.2.15 Clock-out capability

- MCO

The microcontroller clock output (MCO) capability allows the clock to be output onto the external MCO pin. One of eight clock signals can be selected as the MCO clock.

<br>- LSI
<br>- LSE
<br>- SYSCLK
<br>- HSI16
<br>- HSI48
<br>- HSE
<br>- PLLCLK

The selection is controlled by the MCOSEL[3:0] bits of the [Clock configuration register (RCC\_CFGR)](#XREF_64720__7_4_3_Clock_configuration_register_(RCC_CFGR)15). The selected clock can be divided with the MCOPRE[2:0] field of the [Clock configuration register (RCC\_CFGR)](#XREF_64720__7_4_3_Clock_configuration_register_(RCC_CFGR)15).

- LSCO

Another output (LSCO) allows a low speed clock to be output onto the external LSCO pin:

<br>- LSI
<br>- LSE

This output remains available in Stop (Stop 0 and Stop 1) and Standby modes. The selection is controlled by the LSCOSEL, and enabled with the LSCOEN in the [RTC domain control register (RCC\_BDCR)](#XREF_22571__7_4_29_Backup_domain_control_register_(RCC_BDCR)15).

The MCO clock output requires the corresponding alternate function selected on the MCO pin, the LSCO pin should be left in default POR state.

### 7.2.16 Internal/external clock measurement with TIM5/TIM15/TIM16/TIM17

It is possible to indirectly measure the frequency of all on-board clock sources by mean of the TIM5, TIM15, TIM16 or TIM17 channel 1 input capture, as represented on [Figure 19](#XREF_26313__Figure_12__Frequency_measurement_with_TIM14_in_capture_mode15) [Figure 20](#XREF_95168__Figure_13__Frequency_measurement_with_TIM15_in_capture_mode15), [Figure 21](#XREF_24615__Figure_14__Frequency_measurement_with_TIM15_in_capture_mode15) and [Figure 22](#XREF_75306__Figure_19__Frequency_measurement_with_TIM5_in_capture_mode15).

<a id="XREF_26313__Figure_12__Frequency_measurement_with_TIM14_in_capture_mode15"></a>

#### Figure 19. Frequency measurement with TIM15 in capture mode![](MS48963V1.svg)

The input capture channel of the Timer 15 can be a GPIO line or an internal clock of the MCU. The possibilities are the following ones:

- TIM15 Channel1 is connected to the GPIO. Refer to the alternate function mapping in the device datasheets.
- TIM15 Channel1 is connected to the LSE.
<a id="XREF_95168__Figure_13__Frequency_measurement_with_TIM15_in_capture_mode15"></a>

#### Figure 20. Frequency measurement with TIM16 in capture mode![](MS48964V1.svg)

The input capture channel of the Timer 16 can be a GPIO line or an internal clock of the MCU.

The possibilities are the following ones:

- TIM16 Channel1 is connected to the GPIO. Refer to the alternate function mapping in the device datasheets.
- TIM16 Channel1 is connected to the LSI clock.
- TIM16 Channel1 is connected to the LSE clock.
- TIM16 Channel1 is connected to the RTC wake-up interrupt signal. In this case the RTC interrupt should be enabled.
- TIM16 Channel1 is connected to the HSE/32 clock.
- TIM16 Channel1 is connected to the MCO.
<a id="XREF_24615__Figure_14__Frequency_measurement_with_TIM15_in_capture_mode15"></a>

#### Figure 21. Frequency measurement with TIM17 in capture mode![](MSv45849V1.svg)

The input capture channel of Timer 17 can be a GPIO line or an internal clock of the MCU.

The possibilities are the following ones:

- TIM17 Channel1 is connected to the GPIO. Refer to the alternate function mapping in the device datasheets.
- TIM17 Channel1 is connected to the RTC wake-up interrupt. In this case the RTC interrupt should be enabled.
- TIM17 Channel1 is connected to the HSE/32 clock.
- TIM17 Channel1 is connected to the microcontroller clock output (MCO), this selection is controlled by the MCOSEL[3:0] bits of the [Clock configuration register (RCC\_CFGR)](#XREF_64720__7_4_3_Clock_configuration_register_(RCC_CFGR)15).
- TIM17 Channel1 is connected to the LSE clock.
- TIM17 Channel1 is connected to the LSI clock.
<a id="XREF_75306__Figure_19__Frequency_measurement_with_TIM5_in_capture_mode15"></a>

#### Figure 22. Frequency measurement with TIM5 in capture mode![](MSv45853V1.svg)

The input capture channel of the Timer 5 can be a GPIO line or an internal clock of the MCU.

The possibilities are the following ones:

- TIM5 Channel1 is connected to the GPIO. Refer to the alternate function mapping in the device datasheets.
- TIM5 Channel1 is connected to the LSI clock.
- TIM5 Channel1 is connected to the LSE clock.
- TIM5 Channel1 is connected to the RTC wake-up interrupt signal. In this case the RTC interrupt should be enabled.

#### Calibration of the HSI16

For TIM15 and TIM16, the primary purpose of connecting the LSE to the channel 1 input capture is to be able to precisely measure the HSI16 system clocks (for this, the HSI16 should be used as the system clock source). The number of HSI16 clock counts between consecutive edges of the LSE signal provides a measure of the internal clock period. Taking advantage of the high precision of LSE crystals (typically a few tens of ppm’s), it is possible to determine the internal clock frequency with the same resolution, and trim the source to compensate for manufacturing, process, temperature and/or voltage related frequency deviations.

The HSI16 oscillator has dedicated user-accessible calibration bits for this purpose.

The basic concept consists in providing a relative measurement (e.g. the HSI16/LSE ratio): the precision is therefore closely related to the ratio between the two clock sources. The higher the ratio is, the better the measurement is.

If LSE is not available, HSE/32 is the better option in order to reach the most precise calibration possible.

#### Calibration of the LSI

The calibration of the LSI follows the same pattern that for the HSI16, but changing the reference clock. It is necessary to connect LSI clock to the channel 1 input capture of the TIM16. Then define the HSE as system clock source, the number of his clock counts between consecutive edges of the LSI signal provides a measure of the internal low speed clock period.

The basic concept consists in providing a relative measurement (e.g. the HSE/LSI ratio): the precision is therefore closely related to the ratio between the two clock sources. The higher the ratio is, the better the measurement is.

### 7.2.17  Peripheral clock enable register   (RCC\_AHBxENR, RCC\_APBxENRy)

Each peripheral clock can be enabled by the xxxxEN bit of the RCC\_AHBxENR, RCC\_APBxENRy registers.

When the peripheral clock is not active, the peripheral registers read or write accesses are not supported.

The enable bit has a synchronization mechanism to create a glitch free clock for the peripheral. After the enable bit is set, there is a 2 clock cycles delay before the clock be active.

Caution:Just after enabling the clock for a peripheral, software must wait for a delay before accessing the peripheral registers.

## 7.3 Low-power modes

- AHB and APB peripheral clocks, including DMA clock, can be disabled by software.
- Sleep and Low Power Sleep modes stops the CPU clock. The memory interface clocks (Flash and SRAM1, SRAM2 and CCM SRAM interfaces) can be stopped by software during sleep mode. The AHB to APB bridge clocks are disabled by hardware during Sleep mode when all the clocks of the peripherals connected to them are disabled.
- Stop modes (Stop 0 and Stop 1) stops all the clocks in the VCORE domain and disables the PLL, the HSI16, and the HSE oscillators.

All U(S)ARTs, LPUARTs and I2Cs have the capability to enable the HSI16 oscillator even when the MCU is in Stop mode (if HSI16 is selected as the clock source for that peripheral).

All U(S)ARTs and LPUARTs can also be driven by the LSE oscillator when the system is in Stop mode (if LSE is selected as clock source for that peripheral) and the LSE oscillator is enabled (LSEON). In that case the LSE remains always ON in Stop mode (they do not have the capability to turn on the LSE oscillator).

- Standby and Shutdown modes stops all the clocks in the VCORE domain and disables the PLL, the HSI16, and the HSE oscillators.

The CPU’s deepsleep mode can be overridden for debugging by setting the DBG\_STOP or DBG\_STANDBY bits in the DBGMCU\_CR register.

When leaving the Stop modes (Stop 0, Stop 1 or standby), the system clock is HSI16.

If a Flash memory programming operation is on going, Stop, Standby and Shutdown modes entry is delayed until the Flash memory interface access is finished. If an access to the APB domain is ongoing, Stop, Standby and Shutdown modes entry is delayed until the APB access is finished.

## 7.4 RCC registers

<a id="XREF_15554__2_2_6_Clock_control_register_(CLK_CR)15"></a>

### 7.4.1 Clock control register (RCC\_CR)

Address offset: 0x00

Reset value: 0x0000 0500

HSEBYP is not affected by reset.

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.58px"/><col width="500.59px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLRDY</span>: Main PLL clock ready flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware to indicate that the main PLL is locked.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: PLL unlocked</p><p class="TableIndent">1: PLL locked</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLON</span>: Main PLL enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to enable the main PLL.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by hardware when entering Stop, Standby or Shutdown mode. This bit cannot be reset if the PLL clock is used as the system clock.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: PLL OFF</p><p class="TableIndent">1: PLL ON</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CSSON</span>: Clock security system enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by software to enable the clock security system. When CSSON is set, the clock detector is enabled by hardware when the HSE oscillator is ready, and disabled by hardware if a HSE clock failure is detected. This bit is set only and is cleared by reset.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Clock security system OFF (clock detector OFF)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock security system ON (Clock detector ON if the HSE oscillator is stable, OFF if not).</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSEBYP</span>: HSE crystal oscillator bypass</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to bypass the oscillator with an external clock. The external clock must be enabled with the HSEON bit set, to be used by the device. The HSEBYP bit can be written only if the HSE oscillator is disabled. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: HSE crystal oscillator not bypassed</p><p class="TableIndent">1: HSE crystal oscillator bypassed with external clock</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSERDY</span>: HSE clock ready flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware to indicate that the HSE oscillator is stable. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: HSE oscillator not ready</p><p class="TableIndent">1: HSE oscillator ready</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Once the HSEON bit is cleared, HSERDY goes low after 6 HSE clock cycles.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSEON</span>: HSE clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by hardware to stop the HSE oscillator when entering Stop, Standby or Shutdown mode. This bit cannot be reset if the HSE oscillator is used directly or indirectly as the system clock.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: HSE oscillator OFF</p><p class="TableIndent">1: HSE oscillator ON</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSIRDY</span>: HSI16 clock ready flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware to indicate that HSI16 oscillator is stable. This bit is set only when HSI16 is enabled by software by setting HSION. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: HSI16 oscillator not ready</p><p class="TableIndent">1: HSI16 oscillator ready</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Once the HSION bit is cleared, HSIRDY goes low after 6 HSI16 clock cycles.</p></td></tr><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSIKERON</span>: HSI16 always enable for peripheral kernels.</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to force HSI16 ON even in Stop modes. The HSI16 can only feed USARTs and I<sup>2</sup>Cs peripherals configured with HSI16 as kernel clock. Keeping the HSI16 ON in Stop mode allows to avoid slowing down the communication speed because of the HSI16 startup time. This bit has no effect on HSION value.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect on HSI16 oscillator.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: HSI16 oscillator is forced ON even in Stop mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="149.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSION</span>: HSI16 clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by hardware to stop the HSI16 oscillator when entering Stop, Standby or Shutdown mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware to force the HSI16 oscillator ON when STOPWUCK=1 or HSIASFS = 1 when leaving Stop modes, or in case of failure of the HSE crystal oscillator.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware if the HSI16 is used directly or indirectly as system clock.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: HSI16 oscillator OFF</p><p class="TableIndent">1: HSI16 oscillator ON</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.58px"/><col width="500.59px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 30:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSITRIM[6:0]</span>: HSI16 clock trimming</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits provide an additional user-programmable trimming value that is added to the HSICAL[7:0] bits. It can be programmed to adjust to variations in voltage and temperature that influence the frequency of the HSI16.</p><p class="TableIndent">The default value is 64, which, when added to the HSICAL value, trims HSI16 to <br/>16 MHz ± 1 %. </p></td></tr><tr height="69.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSICAL[7:0]</span>: HSI16 clock calibration</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are initialized at startup with the factory-programmed HSI16 calibration trim value. When HSITRIM is written, HSICAL is updated with the sum of HSITRIM and the factory trim value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr></table></div>


<a id="XREF_64720__7_4_3_Clock_configuration_register_(RCC_CFGR)15"></a>

### 7.4.3 Clock configuration register (RCC\_CFGR)

Address offset: 0x08

Reset value: 0x0000 0005

Access: 0 ≤ wait state ≤ 2, word, half-word and byte access

1 or 2 wait states inserted only if the access occurs during clock source switch.

From 0 to 15 wait states inserted if the access occurs when the APB or AHB prescalers values update is on going.

<a id="XREF_26045__7_4_4_PLL_configuration_register_(RCC_PLLCFGR)15"></a>

### 7.4.4 PLL configuration register (RCC\_PLLCFGR)

Address offset: 0x0C

Reset value: 0x0000 1000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

This register is used to configure the PLL clock outputs according to the formulas:

- f(VCO clock) = f(PLL clock input) × (PLLN / PLLM)
- f(PLL\_P) = f(VCO clock) / PLLP
- f(PLL\_Q) = f(VCO clock) / PLLQ
- f(PLL\_R) = f(VCO clock) / PLLR

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.81px"/><col width="498.36px"/><tr height="134.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLPDIV[4:0]</span>: Main PLLP division factor</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to control the PLL “P” frequency. PLL “P” output clock frequency = VCO frequency / PLLPDIV.</p><p class="TableIndent">00000: PLL “P” clock is controlled by the bit PLLP</p><p class="TableIndent">00001: Reserved.</p><p class="TableIndent">00010: PLL “P” clock = VCO / 2</p><p class="TableIndent">....</p><p class="TableIndent">11111: PLL “P” clock = VCO / 31</p></td></tr><tr height="173.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 26:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLR[1:0]</span>: Main PLL division factor for PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>R<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock (system clock)</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to control the frequency of the main PLL output clock PLLCLK. This output can be selected as system clock. These bits can be written only if PLL is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">PLL “R” output clock frequency = VCO frequency / PLLR with PLLR = 2, 4, 6, or 8</p><p class="TableIndent">00: PLLR = 2</p><p class="TableIndent">01: PLLR = 4</p><p class="TableIndent">10: PLLR = 6</p><p class="TableIndent">11: PLLR = 8</p><p class="Caution"><span class="Bold">Caution:<span style="padding-right:20pt ;">​</span></span>These bits must be set so as not to exceed 170 MHz on this domain.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLREN</span>: PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>R<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and reset by software to enable the PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>R<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output of the PLL (used as system clock).</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit cannot be written when PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>R<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output of the PLL is used as System Clock.</p><p class="TableIndent">In order to save power, when the PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>R<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output of the PLL is not used, the value of PLLREN should be 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>R<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>R<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="173.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 22:21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLQ[1:0]</span>: Main PLL division factor for PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>Q<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock.</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to control the frequency of the main PLL output clock PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>Q<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock. This output can be selected for USB, RNG, SAI (48 MHz clock). These bits can be written only if PLL is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>Q<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> output clock frequency = VCO frequency / PLLQ with PLLQ = 2, 4, 6, or 8</p><p class="TableIndent">00: PLLQ = 2</p><p class="TableIndent">01: PLLQ = 4</p><p class="TableIndent">10: PLLQ = 6</p><p class="TableIndent">11: PLLQ = 8</p><p class="Caution"><span class="Bold">Caution:<span style="padding-right:20pt ;">​</span></span>These bits must be set so as not to exceed 170 MHz on this domain.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLQEN</span>: Main PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>Q<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock.</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to control the frequency of the main PLL output clock PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>P<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock. These bits can be written only if PLL is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">When the PLLPDIV[4:0] is set to “00000”PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>P<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> output clock frequency = VCO frequency / PLLP with PLLP =7, or 17</p><p class="TableIndent">0: PLLP = 7</p><p class="TableIndent">1: PLLP = 17</p><p class="Caution"><span class="Bold">Caution:<span style="padding-right:20pt ;">​</span></span>These bits must be set so as not to exceed 170 MHz on this domain.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLPEN</span>: Main PLL PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>P<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and reset by software to enable the PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>P<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output of the PLL.</p><p class="TableIndent">To save power, when the PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>P<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output of the PLL is not used, the value of PLLPEN should be 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>P<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: PLL <span style="font-weight:Bold;">“</span>P<span style="font-weight:Bold;">”</span> clock output enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="238.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 14:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLN[6:0]</span>: Main PLL multiplication factor for VCO</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to control the multiplication factor of the VCO. These bits can be written only when the PLL is disabled. </p><p class="TableIndent">VCO output frequency = VCO input frequency x PLLN with 8 =&lt; PLLN =&lt; 127</p><p class="TableIndent">0000000: PLLN = 0 wrong configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">0000001: PLLN = 1 wrong configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">0000111: PLLN = 7 wrong configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">0001000: PLLN = 8</p><p class="TableIndent">0001001: PLLN = 9</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">1111111: PLLN = 127 </p><p class="Caution"><span class="Bold">Caution:<span style="padding-right:20pt ;">​</span></span>The software must set correctly these bits to assure that the VCO output frequency is within the range defined in the datasheet.</p></td></tr><tr height="289.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="_Table_Body" style="text-align:left;direction:inherit;font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLM[3:0]: </span>Division factor for the main PLL input clock</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to divide the PLL input clock before the VCO. These bits can be written only when all PLLs are disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">VCO input frequency = PLL input clock frequency / PLLM with 1 ≤ PLLM ≤ 16</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: PLLM = 1</p><p class="TableIndent">0001: PLLM = 2</p><p class="TableIndent">0010: PLLM = 3</p><p class="TableIndent">0011: PLLM = 4</p><p class="TableIndent">0100: PLLM = 5</p><p class="TableIndent">0101: PLLM = 6</p><p class="TableIndent">0110: PLLM = 7</p><p class="TableIndent">0111: PLLM = 8</p><p class="TableIndent">1000: PLLSYSM = 9</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">1111: PLLSYSM= 16</p><p class="Caution"><span class="Bold">Caution:<span style="padding-right:20pt ;">​</span></span>The software must set these bits correctly to ensure that the VCO input frequency is within the range defined in the datasheet.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="137.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="_Table_Body" style="text-align:left;direction:inherit;font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PLLSRC</span>[1:0]: Main PLL entry clock source</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and c.leared by software to select PLL clock source. These bits can be written only when PLL is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">In order to save power, when no PLL is used, the value of PLLSRC should be 00.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: No clock sent to PLL</p><p class="TableIndent">01: No clock sent to PLL</p><p class="TableIndent">10: HSI16 clock selected as PLL clock entry</p><p class="TableIndent">11: HSE clock selected as PLL clock entry</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="117.59px"/><col width="496.58px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSI48RDYF</span>: HSI48 ready interrupt flag </p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the HSI48 clock becomes stable and HSI48RDYIE is set in a response to setting the HSI48ON (refer to <a href="#XREF_70221__8_4_31_Clock_recovery_RC_register_(RCC_CRRCR)15" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Clock recovery RC register (RCC_CRRCR)</a>). </p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by software setting the HSI48RDYC bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No clock ready interrupt caused by the HSI48 oscillator</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock ready interrupt caused by the HSI48 oscillator</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">LSECSSF</span>: LSE clock security system interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a failure is detected in the LSE oscillator.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by software setting the LSECSSC bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No clock security interrupt caused by LSE clock failure</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock security interrupt caused by LSE clock failure</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">CSSF</span>: Clock security system interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a failure is detected in the HSE oscillator.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by software setting the CSSC bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No clock security interrupt caused by HSE clock failure</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock security interrupt caused by HSE clock failure</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">PLLRDYF</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">:</span> PLL ready interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the PLL locks and PLLRDYIE is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by software setting the PLLRDYC bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No clock ready interrupt caused by PLL lock</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock ready interrupt caused by PLL lock</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSERDYF</span>: HSE ready interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the HSE clock becomes stable and HSERDYIE is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by software setting the HSERDYC bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No clock ready interrupt caused by the HSE oscillator</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock ready interrupt caused by the HSE oscillator</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSIRDYF</span>: HSI16 ready interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the HSI16 clock becomes stable and HSIRDYIE is set in a response to setting the HSION (refer to <span style="color:#ff0000;"><a href="#XREF_15554__2_2_6_Clock_control_register_(CLK_CR)15" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Clock control register (RCC_CR)</a></span>). When HSION is not set but the HSI16 oscillator is enabled by the peripheral through a clock request, this bit is not set and no interrupt is generated.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by software setting the HSIRDYC bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No clock ready interrupt caused by the HSI16 oscillator</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock ready interrupt caused by the HSI16 oscillator</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSERDYF</span>: LSE ready interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the LSE clock becomes stable and LSERDYIE is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by software setting the LSERDYC bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No clock ready interrupt caused by the LSE oscillator</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock ready interrupt caused by the LSE oscillator</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSIRDYF</span>: LSI ready interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when the LSI clock becomes stable and LSIRDYIE is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by software setting the LSIRDYC bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No clock ready interrupt caused by the LSI oscillator</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clock ready interrupt caused by the LSI oscillator</p></td></tr></table></div>


<a id="XREF_47307__7_4_9_Clock_interrupt_clear_register_(RCC_CICR)15"></a>

### 7.4.7 Clock interrupt clear register (RCC\_CICR)

Address offset: 0x20

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

### 7.4.8 AHB1 peripheral reset register (RCC\_AHB1RSTR)

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

### 7.4.9 AHB2 peripheral reset register (RCC\_AHB2RSTR)

Address offset: 0x2C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

### 7.4.10 AHB3 peripheral reset register (RCC\_AHB3RSTR)

Address offset: 0x30

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

### 7.4.12 APB1 peripheral reset register 2 (RCC\_APB1RSTR2)

Address offset: 0x3C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

### 7.4.13 APB2 peripheral reset register (RCC\_APB2RSTR)

Address offset: 0x40

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

### 7.4.14 AHB1 peripheral clock enable register (RCC\_AHB1ENR)

Address offset: 0x48

Reset value: 0x0000 0100

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

**Note:**

When the peripheral clock is not active, the peripheral registers read or write access is not supported.

This bit can be disabled only when the Flash is in power down mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Flash memory interface clock disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Flash memory interface clock enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FMACEN</span>: FMAC enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and reset by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: FMAC clock disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: FMAC clock enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CORDICEN</span>: CORDIC clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and reset by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CORDIC clock disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: CORDIC clock enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMAMUX1EN</span>: DMAMUX1 clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and reset by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMAMUX1 clock disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMAMUX1 clock enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMA2EN</span>: DMA2 clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMA2 clock disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMA2 clock enable</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMA1EN</span>: DMA1 clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMA1 clock disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMA1 clock enable</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 7.4.15 AHB2 peripheral clock enable register (RCC\_AHB2ENR)

Address offset: 0x4C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

**Note:**

When the peripheral clock is not active, the peripheral registers read or write access is not supported.

### 7.4.16 AHB3 peripheral clock enable register(RCC\_AHB3ENR)

Address offset: 0x50

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

**Note:**

When the peripheral clock is not active, the peripheral registers read or write access is not supported.

### 7.4.17 APB1 peripheral clock enable register 1 (RCC\_APB1ENR1)

Address: 0x58

Reset value: 0x0000 0400

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

**Note:**

When the peripheral clock is not active, the peripheral registers read or write access is not supported.

### 7.4.18 APB1 peripheral clock enable register 2 (RCC\_APB1ENR2)

Address offset: 0x5C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

**Note:**

When the peripheral clock is not active, the peripheral registers read or write access is not supported.

### 7.4.19 APB2 peripheral clock enable register (RCC\_APB2ENR)

Address: 0x60

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: word, half-word and byte access

**Note:**

When the peripheral clock is not active, the peripheral registers read or write access is not supported.

### 7.4.21  AHB2 peripheral clocks enable in Sleep and Stop modes register   (RCC\_AHB2SMENR)

Address offset: 0x70

Reset value: 0x0000 0101

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

### 7.4.23  APB1 peripheral clocks enable in Sleep and Stop modes register 1   (RCC\_APB1SMENR1)

Address: 0x78

Reset value: 0xD2FE CD3F

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

### 7.4.26 Peripherals independent clock configuration register (RCC\_CCIPR)

Address: 0x88

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait states, word, half-word and byte access

<a id="XREF_22571__7_4_29_Backup_domain_control_register_(RCC_BDCR)15"></a>

### 7.4.27 RTC domain control register (RCC\_BDCR)

Address offset: 0x90

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Reset by RTC domain Reset, except LSCOSEL, LSCOEN and BDRST, which are reset only by RTC domain power-on reset.  
Access: 0 ≤ wait state ≤ 3, word, half-word and byte access  
Wait states are inserted in case of successive accesses to this register.

**Note:**

The bits of this register are outside the VCORE domain. As a result, after Reset, they are write-protected and the DBP bit in the [Section 6.4.1: Power control register 1 (PWR\_CR1)](Power_control_%28PWR%29.md#XREF_93563__1_4_1_Power_control_register_1_(PWR_CR1)34) has to be set before these can be modified. Refer to [Section 6.1.3: Battery backup domain on page 230](Power_control_%28PWR%29.md#XREF_30367__7_1_5_Battery_backup_domain34) for further information. These bits (except LSCOSEL, LSCOEN and BDRST) are reset only after an RTC domain reset (see [Section 7.1.3](#XREF_25576__4_1_2_Power_reset15)). Any internal or external reset does not have any effect on these bits.

9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RTCSEL[1:0]</span>: RTC clock source selection</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by software to select the clock source for the RTC. Once the RTC clock source has been selected, it cannot be changed anymore unless the RTC domain is reset, or unless a failure is detected on LSE (LSECSSD is set). The BDRST bit can be used to reset them.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: No clock</p><p class="TableIndent">01: LSE oscillator clock used as RTC clock</p><p class="TableIndent">10: LSI oscillator clock used as RTC clock</p><p class="TableIndent">11: HSE oscillator clock divided by 32 used as RTC clock</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSECSSD:</span> CSS on LSE failure detection</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware to indicate when a failure has been detected by the Clock Security System</p><p class="TableIndent">on the external 32 kHz oscillator (LSE).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No failure detected on LSE (32 kHz oscillator)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Failure detected on LSE (32 kHz oscillator)</p></td></tr><tr height="134.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSECSSON:</span> CSS on LSE enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by software to enable the Clock Security System on LSE (32 kHz oscillator).</p><p class="TableIndent">LSECSSON must be enabled after the LSE oscillator is enabled (LSEON bit enabled) and ready (LSERDY flag set by hardware), and after the RTCSEL bit is selected.</p><p class="TableIndent">Once enabled this bit cannot be disabled, except after a LSE failure detection (LSECSSD</p><p class="TableIndent">=1). In that case the software MUST disable the LSECSSON bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CSS on LSE (32 kHz external oscillator) OFF</p><p class="TableIndent">1: CSS on LSE (32 kHz external oscillator) ON</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSEDRV[1:0]:</span> LSE oscillator drive capability</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by software to modulate the LSE oscillator’s drive capability. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: ‘Xtal mode’ lower driving capability</p><p class="TableIndent">01: ‘Xtal mode’ medium low driving capability</p><p class="TableIndent">10: ‘Xtal mode’ medium high driving capability</p><p class="TableIndent">11: ‘Xtal mode’ higher driving capability </p><p class="TableIndent">The oscillator is in Xtal mode when it is not in bypass mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSEBYP</span>: LSE oscillator bypass</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software to bypass oscillator. This bit can be written only when the external 32 kHz oscillator is disabled (LSEON = 0 and LSERDY = 0).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: LSE oscillator not bypassed</p><p class="TableIndent">1: LSE oscillator bypassed</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSERDY</span>: LSE oscillator ready</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by hardware to indicate when the external 32 kHz oscillator is stable. After the LSEON bit is cleared, LSERDY goes low after six external low-speed oscillator clock cycles.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: LSE oscillator not ready</p><p class="TableIndent">1: LSE oscillator ready</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSEON</span>: LSE oscillator enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: LSE oscillator OFF</p><p class="TableIndent">1: LSE oscillator ON</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 7.4.28 Control/status register (RCC\_CSR)

Address: 0x94

Reset value: 0x0C00 0000

Reset by system Reset, except reset flags by power Reset only.

Access: 0 ≤ wait state ≤ 3, word, half-word and byte access

Wait states are inserted in case of successive accesses to this register.

writing to the RMVF bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No illegal mode reset occurred<br/>1: Illegal mode reset occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 30</p></td><td><p the RMVF bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No window watchdog reset occurred<br/>1: Window watchdog reset occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IWDGRSTF</span>: Independent window watchdog reset flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when an independent watchdog reset domain occurs.<br/>Cleared by writing to the RMVF bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No independent watchdog reset occurred<br/>1: Independent watchdog reset occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SFTRSTF</span>: Software reset flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a software reset occurs.<br/>Cleared by writing to the RMVF bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No software reset occurred<br/>1: Software reset occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BORRSTF</span>: BOR flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a BOR occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing to the RMVF bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No BOR occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: BOR occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PINRSTF</span>: Pin reset flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a reset from the NRST pin occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing to the RMVF bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No reset from NRST pin occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Reset from NRST pin occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OBLRSTF</span>: Option byte loader reset flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by hardware when a reset from the Option Byte loading occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by writing to the RMVF bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No reset from Option Byte loading occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Reset from Option Byte loading occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RMVF</span>: Remove reset flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Set by software to clear the reset flags.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Clear the reset flags</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 22:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSIRDY</span>: LSI oscillator ready</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by hardware to indicate when the LSI oscillator is stable. After the LSION bit is cleared, LSIRDY goes low after 3 LSI oscillator clock cycles. This bit can be set even if LSION = 0 if the LSI is requested by the Clock Security System on LSE, by the Independent Watchdog or by the RTC.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: LSI oscillator not ready</p><p class="TableIndent">1: LSI oscillator ready</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LSION</span>: LSI oscillator enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: LSI oscillator OFF</p><p class="TableIndent">1: LSI oscillator ON</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 7.4.29 Clock recovery RC register (RCC\_CRRCR)

Address: 0x98

Reset value: 0x0000 XXX0

Where X is factory-programmed.

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

This bit is set only when HSI48 is enabled by software by setting HSI48ON.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: HSI48 oscillator not ready</p><p class="TableIndent">1: HSI48 oscillator ready</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HSI48ON</span>: HSI48 clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">Cleared by hardware to stop the HSI48 when entering in Stop, Standby or Shutdown modes.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: HSI48 oscillator OFF</p><p class="TableIndent">1: HSI48 oscillator ON</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 7.4.30 Peripherals independent clock configuration register (RCC\_CCIPR2)

Address: 0x9C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Access: no wait state, word, half-word and byte access

Wait states are inserted in case of successive accesses to this register.
